subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should OpenClaw support these three separate opt-in pre-handshake Gateway hardening modes as a permanent core configuration contract?
rationale: The patch is not only a bounded internal hardening change: it adds public configuration, help text, and security semantics that operators must understand and preserve across future Gateway and proxy changes.

options.title: Adopt the opt-in security modes
options.body: Accept the three flags as core policy, after current-head wire proof demonstrates their rejection and trusted-proxy compatibility behavior.

options.title: Narrow to an existing policy surface
options.body: Ask for a smaller implementation if the existing origin or trusted-proxy configuration can express the intended protection without three additional persistent settings.

options.title: Pause pending Gateway policy design
options.body: Defer this PR if maintainers want a broader reviewed model for browser-origin and proxy-header admission before adding new controls.

recommendation.title: Adopt the opt-in security modes
recommendation.body: Accept the three flags as core policy, after current-head wire proof demonstrates their rejection and trusted-proxy compatibility behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline provides the only concrete maintainer-routing signal for this Gateway security-policy decision.
